Pick lambda_1,...,lambda_t in Lambda which map to elements of A in Lambda-bar such that moreover the images of d lambda_1,...,d lambda_t form a basis of Omega_{F/k}' and 'choose further elements lambda_{t+1},...,lambda_m in Lambda which map into A'. Stacks asserts these choices without argument, and for an arbitrary A they are impossible: Lambda=k[x,y], q=0, n=1, A=k(x/y) is admissible, but k[x,y] meets k(x/y) only in k, while Omega_{A/k} is nonzero; so A must be enlarged. Suggested proof (agent): take a_j in A_0 with d of their residues a basis of Omega_{F_0/k}, and generators b_i of m_{A_0} (n>=2; for n=1 take generators of q), write them as mu/s with a common s in Lambda minus q, and enlarge A_0 according to the residue alpha of s exactly as in the three cases of the proof of Lemma 07FI (alpha transcendental over F_0: A=A_0[s-bar] localized, add s to the lambda's; alpha algebraic: Q=p^e >= n with alpha^Q separable over F_0, a finite etale A over A_0 with residue field F_0(alpha^Q) containing s-bar^N, N a power of p, and use mu s^(N-1), whose differentials are alpha^N d(residue))

title: Admissible enlargement with a residue differential basis and quotient ideal generators
statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, $\Lambda$ a Noetherian $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] geometrically regular over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], $\mathfrak q$ a prime ideal, $n\geq1$, $L=\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak qL$, and $B=L/\mathfrak m^n$. Let $A_0\subseteq B$ be admissible [def-weil-pbc-popescu-admissible-subalgebra], meaning Artinian local, essentially of finite type over $k$, flatly included in $B$, and with its maximal ideal generating $\mathfrak mB$. Then there exist an admissible local $k$-subalgebra $A\subseteq B$ containing $A_0$, integers $t,r\geq0$, elements $\lambda_j\in\Lambda$ ($j\in\operatorname{Fin}(t)$) and $\lambda'_i\in\mathfrak q$ ($i\in\operatorname{Fin}(r)$), and specified lifts $a_j,a'_i\in A$ of their images in $B$, such that there is a basis $b$ of $\Omega_{F/k}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] over $F=A/\mathfrak m_A$ with $b_j=\mathrm d(\operatorname{res}_A(a_j))$, and the images of all $\lambda'_i$ span $\mathfrak mB$ as an ideal of $B$. The last equality concerns the quotient $B$, not the ideal $\mathfrak m$ in $L$. No embedding of $F$ into $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$, contraction identity, or compatibility assertion is part of the conclusion.

proof.text: Use the quotient EssFiniteType instance for F₀ and KaehlerDifferential.finite. Module.Basis.ofSpan extracts a basis from exact differentials; finite-dimensionality makes its index finite. Reindex by Fin t₀ and lift its coefficients through the residue surjection. This is the proved private helper exists_residue_differential_basis.

A₀ is Artinian and therefore Noetherian. Choose a finite generating family z_i of m₀, and map its span into B. Admissibility identifies the resulting ideal with JB. Lift both finite families a₀_j and z_i to L and apply IsLocalization.exist_integer_multiples_of_finite to their disjoint union. Mapping to B gives a common s ∉ q and numerators μ_j and ν_i.

Since J^n ≤ J, the inverse image of JB under L → B is J. Contraction under Λ → L then gives q. Each π(ν_i) = z_i π(s) lies in JB, so ν_i lies in q. Apply the denominator-basis enlargement to the initial basis and common denominator. Obtain A containing A₀, its differential basis lifted from xs in Λ, and c ∈ A with value π(s)^N for N ≥ 1.

Construct ys_i = ν_i s^(N-1) ∈ q and a′_i = image_A(z_i) c. Ring-map multiplicativity and N ≥ 1 give π(ys_i) = z_i π(s)^N = a′_i. The element π(s)^N is a unit because s ∉ q. The span of a finite family is unchanged by multiplying every element by a unit, so the π(ys_i) span JB. Combine this family with the xs and basis already obtained. This works uniformly for n = 1, t₀ = 0, and zero quotient maximal ideal.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_popescu_admissible_quotient_basis
    (k : Type u) (Λ : Type v) [Field k] [CommRing Λ] [Algebra k Λ]
    [IsNoetherianRing Λ] (p : ℕ) [CharP k p] (hp : 0 < p)
    (hreg : IsGeometricallyRegular k Λ) (q : Ideal Λ) [q.IsPrime]
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n)
    (A₀ : Subalgebra k (Localization.AtPrime q ⧸
      (q.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q))) ^ n))
    (hA₀ : A₀.IsPopescuAdmissible ((q.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q))).map
      (Ideal.Quotient.mk ((q.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q))) ^ n)))) :
    ∃ (A : Subalgebra k (Localization.AtPrime q ⧸
        (q.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q))) ^ n)) (_ : IsLocalRing A),
      A₀ ≤ A ∧
      A.IsPopescuAdmissible ((q.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q))).map
        (Ideal.Quotient.mk ((q.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q))) ^ n))) ∧
        ∃ (t r : ℕ) (xs : Fin t → Λ) (ys : Fin r → Λ)
          (a : Fin t → A) (a' : Fin r → A),
          (∀ j, (a j : Localization.AtPrime q ⧸
            (q.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q))) ^ n) =
            Ideal.Quotient.mk ((q.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q))) ^ n)
              (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q) (xs j))) ∧
          (∀ i, ys i ∈ q ∧ (a' i : Localization.AtPrime q ⧸
            (q.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q))) ^ n) =
            Ideal.Quotient.mk ((q.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q))) ^ n)
              (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q) (ys i))) ∧
          (∃ b : Module.Basis (Fin t) (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)
              (KaehlerDifferential k (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)),
            ∀ j, b j = KaehlerDifferential.D k (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)
              (IsLocalRing.residue A (a j))) ∧
          Ideal.span (Set.range (fun i ↦
            Ideal.Quotient.mk ((q.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q))) ^ n)
              (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q) (ys i)))) =
            (q.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q))).map
              (Ideal.Quotient.mk ((q.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q))) ^ n))
